source.title: Attribution Patching: Activation Patching At Industrial Scale

record.tranche_reason: It compares attribution patching with activation patching on the GPT-2 Small IOI example and reports qualitative results about the circuit and the approximation.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative patching and path-patching findings, but no numerical outcomes for the IOI experiments. Its discussion of possible prompts, metrics and future applications is not itself a tested result.
record.test_reason: A different method (gradient-based attribution patching and direct attribution path patching) is applied to the GPT-2 Small IOI example. The author reports that it recovers the broad strokes and some key edges of the IOI circuit. That bears qualitatively on V4 and weakly on V1. All evidence is qualitative (scatter plots, heatmaps) from one clean/corrupted prompt pair.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author presents attribution patching as a fast, flawed, hypothesis-generating approximation to activation patching. It is decent for small activations such as head outputs, bad for residual streams and MLP0, and recovers the broad strokes of the IOI circuit in GPT-2 Small. It is not meant to replace rigorous methods such as causal scrubbing.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the original IOI activation-patching setup and metric as a comparison, while introducing gradient-based attribution patching as an approximation and applying direct attribution path patching.
record.method_sensitivity: Approximation quality varies by activation type: residual streams and MLP0 are poor cases, while other layer outputs, head outputs and zoomed-in head activations are described as good cases.

fits_no_version.finding: The linear (gradient) approximation to activation patching is poor for large activations (residual stream, MLP0) and good for head-level activations, which the author attributes to LayerNorm and to MLP0 acting as an extended embedding.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fidelity of attribution patching to activation patching depends on patch size and position in GPT-2 Small IOI.

record.problems: The IOI evidence is qualitative, with no numerical comparisons or uncertainty estimates in the text. The author says the work is incomplete and that the path-patching results were explored less than desired. The investigation uses a narrow IOI prompt setting and does not establish the full circuit criteria.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible reported results were left out.

untested.parts: Faithfulness, completeness and minimality; the full set of 26 heads and 7 classes.
Entirely: no ablation of name movers or measure of compensation is run here; backup behaviour is cited from prior work.
Entirely: only GPT-2 Small; other models are proposed as future work.
Other discovery methods (e.g. ACDC, causal scrubbing), ablation types and metrics; only attribution vs activation patching on one prompt pair is compared.
Entirely: no variation of ablation, metric or prompt distribution for circuit faithfulness or completeness. Metric discussion is argument only.
Entirely: a single clean/corrupted IOI pair; name order, templates and ABC variants are only suggested.

missing.what: Filtering the top positive/negative paths recovers '(some) key edges in the IOI circuit'; the head-pair heatmap is sparse.
Rank comparison of heads between attribution and activation patching (scatter coloured by activation-patch value); no result is stated in the text.
Attribution patching flags redundant/backup heads as important even though activation patching would show compensation (a qualitative method discrepancy).
Single-prompt noise: the folded LayerNorm bias boosts John by about 1 of a total logit difference of 3.

record.verdict_notes: This is an incomplete-project blog post. All IOI evidence is qualitative plots in a notebook, from a single prompt pair, with no numbers. Rows r2-r6 compare the study's own method with activation patching; they are kept only for V4 as method agreement. The V5 links were removed because approximation fidelity is not circuit faithfulness or completeness. The backup-head statement (r7) and the 'IOI work too specific' critique are citation and discussion, not results.

versions.untested_parts: It does not establish that the full 26-head, 7-class circuit meets faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
No quantitative measure of how well backup heads restore IOI performance is reported.
No other models, sizes, checkpoints or task reuse are tested.
The comparison concerns attribution patching versus activation patching on this GPT-2 Small IOI example; it does not compare a broad range of circuit-finding methods, ablation types or metrics.
The reported empirical sensitivity is by activation type. The post does not empirically vary ablation type, metric or prompt distribution.
No systematic comparison across name orders, templates or numbers of names is reported.
